decisions.title: A very brief possession
decisions.situation: A soap bubble floats past your nose. You reach for it. Your new favourite thing has already resigned.

choices.label: Go after the next one
Watch where it goes
Complain about the disappearing bubble

result.title: Plenty of vacancies
result.body: There are more bubbles. You spend several happy minutes failing to keep any of them.

journal.text: I chased soap bubbles and caught absolutely nothing.

decisions.title: Heavy traffic
decisions.situation: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.

choices.label: Crouch down and watch
Give it plenty of room
Challenge it to a race

result.title: Eventually, the other side
result.body: It reaches the edge and disappears under a leaf. You remain impressed by all the feet.

journal.text: I watched a caterpillar cross a path.

decisions.title: Price check on your dignity
decisions.situation: In a quiet shop, you loudly announce that Valeria has a bottom. Several shoppers appear to know already.

choices.label: Repeat it for anyone who missed it
Try an extremely loud whisper
Give Valeria a hug

result.title: Full coverage
result.body: Valeria finishes shopping at record speed.

journal.text: I made a loud announcement about Valeria in a shop.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: Unexpected extra sleeves
decisions.situation: You put on what you think is your jacket. Your hands vanish into the sleeves. Valeria is looking for theirs.

choices.label: Check the name and hand it back
Perform a brief long-armed dance
Insist you have suddenly grown smaller

result.title: The right fit
result.body: Valeria helps find your jacket. Your hands reappear.

journal.text: I returned Valeria’s jacket after taking it by mistake.

decisions.title: Hotel living room
decisions.situation: You ask Valeria whether you can camp in the living room. Your packing list contains six cushions and no clothes.

choices.label: Help make a proper sleeping spot
Ask Valeria to camp too
Decide your bed is better

result.title: Room with a sofa
result.body: Valeria helps you set up, then checks on you before bed.

journal.text: I camped in the living room with Valeria’s help.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Valeria plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of
Trade one song each
Give a brutally concise review

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Valeria.

journal.text: I listened to Valeria’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: A disappointing lunch
decisions.situation: Valeria Romero (classmate) opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Valeria Romero (teacher) is nearby.

choices.label: Quietly ask Valeria Romero (teacher) for help
Ask Valeria Romero (classmate) what would help
Announce it across the table

result.title: Lunch gets sorted
result.body: Valeria Romero (teacher) helps without making an announcement. Valeria Romero (classmate) looks relieved.

journal.text: I quietly got Valeria Romero (teacher)’s help when Valeria Romero (classmate) had no lunch.

decisions.title: The cable is in your hand
decisions.situation: Valeria announces that their charger has been missing for three days. You look down. Their charger is in your hand. There is still time to make this worse.

choices.label: Hand over the evidence
Negotiate a shared charging spot
Say “What charger?” without hiding it

result.title: Found at the scene
result.body: Valeria accepts the charger and your apology. Three days of mystery ends in approximately two seconds.

journal.text: I returned Valeria’s charger and admitted forgetting about it.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

choices.label: Ask whether anyone actually knows
Mute it and step away
Forward it for a reaction

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Valeria drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

choices.label: Turn it into useful feedback
Keep the joke between you
Read it aloud in class

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Sofía helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Valeria turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Valeria secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Make them delete the recording
Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Valeria deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Valeria delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Valeria is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Valeria
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Valeria says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Valeria’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Read at 10:42
decisions.situation: Valeria sends “Where are you?” You are somewhere perfectly ordinary, but the fourth message arrives before you finish typing.

choices.label: Reply, then talk about check-ins
Send a spectacularly boring photo
Ignore all four

result.title: A workable arrangement
result.body: You agree on a check-in time. Valeria admits the silence worried them.

journal.text: I agreed on clearer check-ins with Valeria.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: Wealth you cannot see
decisions.situation: A free gallery in Barcelona displays an empty plinth titled “My Invisible Yacht”. A visitor says only rich people can understand it. You can see the same amount of yacht as everyone else.

choices.label: Ask the guide what the work means
Admire its excellent fuel economy
Pretend to fall overboard

result.title: A surprisingly useful explanation
result.body: The guide says it is about status and imaginary ownership. The visitor looks relieved that somebody has supplied an answer.

journal.text: I asked about an invisible-yacht artwork in Barcelona.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Barcelona, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Barcelona.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Barcelona unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Barcelona.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Valeria sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Valeria remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Valeria also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: Reply all
decisions.situation: You meant to send “Is that wig on backwards?” to one person. It lands in the whole public-meeting chat. The wig’s owner is typing.

choices.label: Apologise before the typing stops
Claim you meant your own wig
Keep reopening the chat in horror

result.title: An honest public disaster
result.body: You admit it was rude. The owner replies, “It is on correctly.” Nobody asks which part you meant to apologise for.

journal.text: I apologised after sending a rude wig comment to a group chat.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
Say you need a short break
Deliver the sharp reply

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: Beginners’ self-defence
decisions.situation: At a free beginner lesson, the instructor asks you to demonstrate a firm “No!” You give one so convincing that a passer-by apologises and leaves.

choices.label: Practise the rest of the lesson
Watch the demonstrations first
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon
result.body: You learn the basics and repeat the shout. The corridor remains unusually clear for the rest of the lesson.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Barcelona offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: Apparently you ate
decisions.situation: A younger person points at your outfit and says, “You ate.” You have no food on you. They add, “No crumbs.” This is getting less clear.

choices.label: Ask whether this is a compliment
Reply, “Thank you. It was delicious.”
Announce that you can feed yourself

result.title: Breakfast has nothing to do with it
result.body: It is a compliment. You thank them and ask for a translation before anyone says anything else about your digestion.

journal.text: I asked someone to explain a slang compliment about my outfit.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

choices.label: Ask why this needs to happen today
Describe a bad decision of your own
Begin with everything wrong with their generation

result.title: The appointment can wait
result.body: Talking reveals a fresh argument and a powerful urge to make it permanent. You suggest a decision that survives sleeping on it.

journal.text: I listened before advising someone about an impulsive tattoo.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Admit your taste has improved
Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: a prolonged low mood and loss of interest. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.
